content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is ready for review:

- Specification: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md)
- Quality checklist: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks`

All quality checks passed with no unresolved clarifications. The draft assumes a private, account-based web app with folders, tags, favorites, search, sorting, and bookmark maintenance. Sharing, import/export, extensions, and offline use are excluded from the first release.

Please approve the specification or describe any changes. I’ll only begin the implementation plan after approval.

This is looking close to what I had in mind — saving links, searching, tags, folders, favorites, editing, and the duplicate warning all sound right, and I'm fine leaving out sharing, import/export, extensions, and offline use for now.

One thing I do want to flag before you plan the build. The way it reads, I'd have to type in a title myself every time I save a link. When I'm saving a page, I really just want to paste the web address and have the app fill in the page's title (and its little site icon) for me automatically — I can always tweak the title afterward if I want. Having to hand-type a title for every single bookmark would make saving feel like a chore, which is the opposite of what I'm after. Can we make automatic title capture part of this first version?

Everything else in here matches what I want, so if we can sort out that automatic-title point, I'll be happy to approve.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for approval on branch `001-manage-bookmarks`.

Key decisions include:

- Node 24 LTS, React 19.3, Vite, and Fastify in one deployable process. ([Node releases](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases), [React versions](https://react.dev/versions), [Fastify documentation](https://fastify.dev/docs/latest/))
- SQLite with Drizzle and Better Auth for accounts, sessions, and recovery. ([Better Auth](https://better-auth.com/docs/authentication/email-password))
- SSRF-protected metadata retrieval with automatic fallbacks. ([OWASP guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html))
- Transactional substring search, cursor pagination, user isolation, and persistent validated site icons.
- Layered unit, integration, security, scale, and browser testing.

Artifacts:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/plan.md)
- [Research decisions](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/data-model.md)
- [API contract](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [UI state contract](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/contracts/ui-states.md)
- [Quickstart and validation guide](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/quickstart.md)

The API contract validates successfully, all design documents are formatted, and no unresolved clarifications remain. Following the planning gate, I created neither application code nor `tasks.md`.

Please approve the plan or request changes. Once approved, I’ll generate the dependency-ordered task breakdown.

A lot of this is technical detail I'll trust you on — the specific tools and libraries aren't something I can judge. What matters to me is that it still does what we agreed: paste a link and get the title and icon filled in automatically (with a sensible fallback when a page can't be read), keep my library private to my account, and let me search, tag, sort, organize into folders, favorite, edit, and delete with a confirmation. From your summary that all seems to be accounted for.

Go ahead and prepare the task breakdown.

content:
Implementation is complete and ready for review at **http://maker:4000**.

Review credentials:

- Email: `review@example.test`
- Password: `bookmark-review-password`

Delivered:

- Private accounts and password recovery
- URL-only saving with automatic title/icon capture and safe fallbacks
- Duplicate warnings
- Search, tags, folders, sorting, and favorites
- Full editing, metadata retry, and confirmed deletion
- Persistent SQLite storage
- Responsive desktop/mobile interface

Validation passed: lint, type checking, 60 automated tests, 8 desktop/mobile browser journeys, production build, OpenAPI validation, and zero dependency vulnerabilities. External SMTP delivery remains deployment-dependent; its in-memory recovery flow was verified.

See [README.md](/work/README.md) and the completed [task breakdown](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/tasks.md).

I signed in and took the app through everything that matters to me, and it holds up:

- **Saving with just a link** works — I pasted an address with no title and it saved fine, giving it a sensible fallback name and a plain icon rather than choking or showing a broken image.
- **Duplicate protection** works — saving the same address again warned me it was already there and pointed me to the existing one.
- **Finding things** works — search, filtering by folder, tag, and favorites, and sorting by title all returned what I expected.
- **Organizing and maintaining** works — I added notes, a folder, and tags, favorited an item, edited its title (my edit stuck and wasn't overwritten), and deleting asked to be confirmed and then actually removed the item everywhere.
- **Privacy and persistence** are in place — everything stayed put and my library is tied to my own account.

One note, not a blocker: on the links I tried, the automatic title/icon pull didn't complete — it looked like this review setup couldn't reach the outside pages, so it fell back every time. The important part for me is that saving never got stuck and I always got a usable, editable bookmark, which is exactly the safety net we agreed on. I'm trusting your report that the capture itself succeeds against pages it can reach.

This does what I set out to build. I'm happy to accept it.
